summary:
Turn 21 resolved the observable half of the accept-status Candidate negatively and paused it with explicit resume conditions, keeping the normative half open instead of inventing a requirement.

Reasoning added this turn. In handlePrepareReply the running maximum is seeded from the record's old vbal and immediately raised to the newly made ballot by the recovering replica's own entry, because startRecoveryForInstance assigns inst.vbal = lastTriedBallot before building that reply. Every reply whose VBallot is below the new ballot therefore fails element.VBallot >= lb.ballot and is skipped. An accept-only acceptor's command-less record at the accepted vbal is one of those skipped replies, so it cannot be preferred over an equal-vbal reply that carries the value. The outcome shape this question predicted is instead produced by the sibling mechanism already confirmed for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector: the recovery ignores all older-vbal replies and can commit a vector no other replica holds. The other status consumer, findPreAcceptConflicts' already-ACCEPTED shortcut, is unreachable dead code, and recovery sub-case 2 needs a record that is itself ACCEPTED, which only the leader-side accept branch produces.

Product. The Candidate is paused on its original proposition with scoped conditions that would reopen it: a source fixing the intended acceptor status semantics for this corrected EPaxos variant, or an in-repository caller that distinguishes ACCEPTED from PREACCEPTED outside the guards already shown to be dead or leader-only. Its unknowns now record what is settled (no decision found to depend on the acceptor's status) and what is not (whether the omission is a normative deviation from the corrected acceptor rules). The confirmed C1 finding is cited as the sibling mechanism rather than merged into this question, so the distinction between a leader that ignores a reported commit and an acceptor that never records that it accepted stays intact.

State. Audit spec version 5; the map handoff, the confirmed claim and its three reviewed checks are untouched; no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
